title: Regime-Dependent Breakdown of LCDM Across Cosmic Time
description: Combines low-z galaxy dynamics (SPARC) with high-z galaxy abundances (JWST COSMOS-Web) to test whether deviations from standard ΛCDM predictions cluster by observational regime. Using a descriptive L0–L3 taxonomy and a pre-specified chi-squared/permutation framework, the paper finds significant, monotonic high-z excesses and structured low-z rotation-curve deviations, rejecting uniform randomness (χ²=47.3, df=4, p≈1.3e-9). The result is robust to photometric-redshift resampling and conservative systematic stress tests.

chi_squared.description: Test statistic used to assess whether observed deviations cluster non-uniformly across predefined regimes (O_i observed counts, E_i expected under uniform assignment; k is the number of regime cells).

velocity_ratio.description: Rotation-curve deviation metric at the outer radius in SPARC galaxies, comparing observed circular velocity to the baryonic-predicted velocity.

abundance_ratio.description: High-redshift abundance excess relative to forward-modeled ΛCDM predictions (Behroozi et al. 2019) or to absolute halo-abundance limits.

key_results.main_finding: Deviation signals cluster by regime with χ²=47.3 (df=4, p≈1.3×10⁻⁹), and high-z galaxy abundances rise monotonically above predictions (≈23–529× vs Behroozi; exceeding halo limits for z>8), robust to photo-z resampling and conservative systematics.
parameters_tested: Uniformity of deviations across L0–L3 regimes
SPARC rotation-curve deviation classes by morphology/dynamics
High-z abundance ratios vs Behroozi (2019) predictions
Sensitivity to stellar-mass calibration shifts and cosmic variance

kill_criteria: KC1: Spectroscopic follow-up of COSMOS-Web high-z candidates (z>8) reduces the abundance excess such that the observed-to-halo-limit ratio R_n ≤ 1.0 in all z>8 bins after vetted completeness and Eddington-bias corrections.

KC2: A preregistered re-analysis using the same L0–L3 regime boundaries and test statistic on updated COSMOS-Web and independent deep fields (e.g., JADES, CEERS, PRIMER) yields p ≥ 0.05 (chi-squared and permutation tests), failing to reject uniformity.

KC3: Independently validated systematics (photo-z errors, mass calibration, selection, and cosmic variance) jointly account for the high-z excess, bringing R_n ≤ 3 across all 5≤z≤10 bins relative to Behroozi (2019), eliminating the reported monotonic trend.

KC4: A hierarchical re-analysis of SPARC with updated distances, inclinations, beam-smearing corrections, and stellar M/L shows no morphology/dynamics-dependent clustering in R_V (posterior consistent with uniform deviations across regimes at p ≥ 0.05).
KC5: Applying the preregistered regime test to future JWST/NGRST/Euclid datasets shows no transition to halo-limit exceedance (R_n ≤ 1.5) at z>8, contradicting the reported regime boundary.
abstract_short: ΛCDM deviations cluster systematically across redshifts (χ²=47.3, df=4, p<10⁻⁸). JWST/COSMOS galaxies exceed predictions by 23-529× depending on redshift.
